title: Quick Ways to Calm Down
hook: When stress spikes, you can't think your way calm — but you can breathe your way there. A few simple tools work in minutes, anywhere.
key_points: Slow breathing, especially a longer exhale, helps switch off the stress response.
Grounding your senses pulls you out of spiraling thoughts and into the present.
A short walk or moving your body burns off stress chemistry.
These are in-the-moment tools, not a substitute for treating ongoing anxiety.
content_html: When stress or panic hits, advice to "calm down" is useless — your body is in fight-or-flight, not in a mood to be reasoned with. The NHS points to a faster route: simple physical tools that quiet the stress response directly, without needing to talk yourself out of it.
extra_html: The NHS recommends slow, controlled breathing as a first move: breathe in gently and let the out-breath be slow and a little longer, which helps switch off the body's stress response and settles a racing heart within minutes. Grounding works alongside it — noticing what you can see, hear, and feel around you pulls your attention out of anxious thought loops and back into the present. Gentle movement helps too; a short walk or simply changing your environment burns off some of the stress chemistry and breaks the spiral. These are reliable in-the-moment tools, and they're worth practicing when you're calm so they're ready when you're not. They aren't a replacement for treating ongoing anxiety — if stress or panic is frequent or overwhelming, talk to a clinician. In the US, you can call or text 988 to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.

related.title: What Stress Does to Your Body
related.hook: A jolt of stress is useful — it sharpens you for a real threat. The problem is when the alarm never switches off, and the body pays for staying on high alert.

related.title: Spotting and Beating Burnout
related.hook: Burnout isn't just being tired — it's exhaustion, cynicism, and feeling ineffective, and it comes from chronic stress you haven't been able to offload.

related.title: Building Everyday Resilience
related.hook: Resilience isn't a personality you're born with — it's a set of habits and connections you can build, the way you build a muscle.

related.title: TIPP: Four Skills for When You're Too Distressed to Think
related.hook: When emotion is so intense you can't reason your way calm, a clinical psychologist's go-to is TIPP — four body-based moves that lower the intensity fast enough to think again.

flashcards.prompt: Why does slow breathing help you calm down in the moment?
flashcards.back_html: Slow, steady breathing — especially a longer, gentle exhale — helps switch off the body's stress response, easing tension, a racing heart, and panicky feelings within a few minutes.

flashcards.prompt: Which is a quick, in-the-moment way to calm a stress spike?

choices.text: Slow breathing with a longer exhale
Holding your breath as long as possible
Speeding up and breathing as fast as you can

flashcards.explanation_html: The NHS recommends slow, controlled breathing — particularly a longer exhale — to ease stress and tension in the moment.
